SPX.label: S&P 500
SPX.source: Polygon daily bar, Friday cash settle, 7718.60, down 29.11 points or -0.376% from Thursday's 7747.71. Session high 7742.22. This is the number that should govern how the jobs report is discussed: the August employment print beat the consensus by more than a hundred thousand jobs, was read as raising the odds of a Federal Reserve hike, and the broad US equity market responded by falling about a third of one percent. Friday-to-Friday the index gained 0.089% - a flat week. NOT ATH: the cash index sits -1.031% below its record close of 7798.99 set 8/13/26 and -1.255% below the 7816.70 record intraday high from that same session. Friday's own high of 7742.22 was 74 points short of the record high. No futures board exists at this hour on a Saturday, so this tile carries the cash index rather than a fabricated overnight quote.

NDX.label: Nasdaq 100
NDX.source: Polygon daily bar, Friday cash settle, 29544.16, up 61.84 points or +0.210%, session high 29655.22. The Nasdaq 100 was the only one of the four US boards to close green, and the reason is entirely composition: semiconductors ripped while Tesla, Apple and Microsoft fell hard. Week Friday-to-Friday +0.376%. NOT ATH: -3.641% below the 6/2/26 record close of 30660.60 and -3.960% below the 6/3/26 record high of 30762.20. Friday's own high of 29655.22 finished 1107 points below that record high, so no part of the session touched a record. Three months on, the June high still stands. Freshness caveat recorded honestly: every close panel located this run carried the Nasdaq COMPOSITE (26506.99, -0.290%) rather than the Nasdaq 100, so this level rests on the Polygon primary daily bar alone and was not independently corroborated by a second published source.

SOX.label: Philadelphia Semis
SOX.source: Polygon daily bar, Friday cash settle, 11735.26, up 383.13 points or +3.375%, session high 11750.25 - so it closed within 15 points of its high. This is the signature number of the week and it is a genuine breadth event: all 30 constituents closed higher. The driver was a memory and storage up-cycle bid rather than the usual AI-GPU trade, and the arithmetic proves it - the two heaviest AI names barely moved, NVIDIA +0.84% and Broadcom +0.21%, so the index move came from the equipment and mid-cap cohort. Largest reported percentage gainers: KLA +7.32%, Marvell +7.05%, AMD +4.69%, Intel +4.51%, Applied Materials +4.31%, ASML +4.17%. NOT ATH, and not close - even after a 3.4% session the index is -19.81% below its record close of 14634.72 set 6/22/26. A one-day move of this size closes roughly a sixth of that gap. Week Friday-to-Friday +2.316%, the best of any board.

DJI.label: Dow Jones Ind
DJI.source: Polygon daily bar, Friday cash settle, 53414.25, down 271.86 points or -0.506% - the worst of the four US boards, which is the correct signature for a session that repriced interest rates higher. The Dow carries no semiconductor weight to offset it and it holds the two largest single-name drags in Apple, down 2.51%. Week Friday-to-Friday -0.272%, the only major board down on the week. NOT ATH: -1.720% below the record close of 54349.12 set 8/5/26. The Russell 2000 gained 0.248% to 2975.65 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.290% to 26506.99, so breadth on the day was mixed rather than uniformly negative.

VIX.label: VIX
VIX.source: Cboe VIX, Friday settle, 14.53, up 0.21 points or +1.47% from Thursday's 14.32. That is the entire volatility response to a payrolls report that beat every estimate in Bloomberg's survey and pushed the 2-year Treasury yield to its highest level since January 2025 intraday. A fifth of a point. The index has now spent six weeks inside a 14 to 16 band and Friday did not disturb it. Week Friday-to-Friday +0.693%. The Nasdaq analogue VXN settled 20.04, DOWN 0.595% from 20.16 - falling on the day, which matters for the carry-unwind test applied on the yen tiles below: index volatility is not confirming any funding stress. This is the cheapest hedging environment of the last month going into a CPI print that the Federal Reserve has publicly said will decide its September vote.

US10Y.label: US 10Y Yield
US10Y.source: US 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield, 4.78%, up 1 basis point from Thursday's 4.77%, from the US Treasury daily par yield curve for 09/04/2026. Investing.com's 10-year page, stamped 'Closed 04/09', read 4.784 and corroborates. Read this tile as a LEVEL - the percentage figure shown is the change in the yield itself, not a basis-point count. One basis point is the honest description of the long end's reaction to a hundred-thousand-job upside surprise, and that restraint is the point: the market did not reprice the terminal rate or the inflation path, it repriced the near-term policy path. Intraday the 10-year did trade as high as 4.802% before paring, per newswire prints, having been FALLING before 8:30. Full Friday curve: 3-month 3.91, 1-year 4.13, 2-year 4.37, 5-year 4.54, 10-year 4.78, 30-year 5.24.

US2Y.label: US 2Y Yield
US2Y.source: US 2-year Treasury constant-maturity yield, 4.37%, up 3 basis points from Thursday's 4.34%, from the same Treasury daily par yield curve file - deliberately the same basis as the 10-year tile so the two legs are comparable. The front end moved three times the long end, which is exactly right: the 2-year is the Fed-expectations instrument. That puts 2s10s at 41 basis points against 43 on Thursday - bear flattening, the textbook response to a hawkish data surprise. The intraday extreme is the more dramatic and equally true reading: the 2-year touched 4.416%, its highest since January 2025, roughly 8 basis points up, before paring into the close. Both numbers are published because both are real at their own timestamps. Freshness discipline: Investing.com's 2-year page was serving 4.404 under a 'Real-time Data 08:39:59' clock on a Saturday, pinned to the exact top of its own 4.331-4.404 day range. Rejected as a day-high artifact.

WTI.label: WTI Crude
WTI.source: WTI front-month crude, $91.48, up 0.20% from Thursday's $91.30 settle, Friday range $88.72 to $92.17. Contract month re-verified independently this run rather than assumed, per the standing rule. Note the shape rather than the change: a 3.45-dollar intraday range that finished 18 cents higher is a market that went somewhere and came back. Crude in the low nineties is the single most consequential input to next Friday's CPI report, and the retail evidence is already extreme - the AAA national average for diesel set a record at $5.85 a gallon this week, against $3.71 a year ago. That is a freight-cost pass-through that shows up in goods prices with a lag, and it is the specific reason the August inflation print carries upside risk.

BRENT.label: Brent Crude
BRENT.source: Brent front-month, $96.28, up 0.80% from Thursday's $95.52, Friday range $93.17 to $96.56 - it closed within 28 cents of the session high, a firmer finish than WTI. Contract month confirmed separately from WTI. The Brent-WTI spread widened to about $4.80 from $4.22, which is the tell worth naming: a widening spread with both legs higher points at seaborne supply risk rather than at US demand. Brent above $96 with the VIX at 14.53 remains the standing tension on this board - the equity market has priced Gulf risk to almost nothing while the physical crude market has not. The United States is drafting a post-conflict Middle East strategy whose timing hinges partly on Israel's October 27 election, so the policy path is unresolved.

GOLD.label: Gold
GOLD.source: Gold futures, $4,476.60, DOWN 1.39% from Thursday's $4,539.90, Friday range $4,412.00 to $4,537.80 - it closed in the lower third of a wide range and this was the largest single-day fall in the metal in three weeks. The logic is clean and worth stating for once, because gold's moves so often resist explanation: a payrolls beat that raises the odds of a rate HIKE raises the real yield on the dollar, and gold pays no coupon. Silver fell 1.41% to $66.75 alongside, so the whole precious complex moved together rather than this being gold-specific. The cross-check confirms it: the dollar index rose 0.25% to 99.16 on the same session. A firmer dollar with weaker gold is the ordinary rate-driven configuration, not the debasement trade.

BTC.label: Bitcoin
BTC.source: Bitcoin, $79,677.42, from the consolidated crypto feed stamped 11:11:36 UTC this morning - the ONLY live tile on this weekend board, because crypto is the only one of these markets open. Basis note, because it governs how the percentage on this tile should be read: it is deliberately quoted against THURSDAY's $81,263.99 close, the same reference every other tile on this board uses, so the -1.95% shown is the move since Thursday rather than an overnight change. The overnight change is separately almost exactly zero - Friday's Polygon UTC-day close was $79,675.12 and the live print is $79,677.42, up 0.003%. Two-source agreement is explicit: the feed's own stated previous close of $79,676.33 sits within two dollars of the Polygon bar. The recent daily path: 8/31 $78,566, 9/1 $77,399, 9/2 $77,305, 9/3 $81,264, 9/4 $79,675. So Thursday's 5% jump on the dovish Waller speech has been roughly half given back on the rate repricing - the cleanest illustration available of Bitcoin currently trading as a dollar-liquidity instrument.

EURJPY.label: EUR/JPY
EURJPY.source: Euro-yen, 181.47, up 0.275% on Friday from 180.973, from the Polygon UTC-day close and corroborated by the consolidated feed at 181.55. The daily move is noise; the WEEK is the story. Friday-to-Friday euro-yen fell 2.246%, from 185.64 to 181.47. Dollar-yen fell 2.384% over the same window, from 160.062 to 156.246, and almost the entire move happened in one session - Wednesday's 158.893 to Thursday's 155.634, a 2.05% single-day yen appreciation. The proximate cause is Bank of Japan pricing into the September 17-18 meeting, not a global risk event. Friday partially reversed it as US yields rose. Japan's currency officials have said they remain in constant contact with US authorities, which keeps two-way intervention risk live.

AUDJPY.label: AUD/JPY
AUDJPY.source: Aussie-yen, 112.52, up 0.413% on Friday from 112.057, week Friday-to-Friday DOWN 1.832% from 114.62. Applying the funding-squeeze test explicitly, as the standing rule requires, because this week's yen move does trip the first condition: the crosses fell 1.8% to 2.4% on the week while euro-dollar ROSE 0.268% and the dollar index rose on Friday - so yen strength is showing up on the crosses against a firm dollar, which is the carry-unwind signature. Now the magnitude check, which is where it fails. VXN is 20.04 and FALLING, equities finished the week flat to higher, the whole move was one session, and Friday reversed part of it. Calibration reference: the August 2024 unwind took dollar-yen from 161 to 141.70 in three weeks with VXN at 28 to 30. Verdict: real yen repricing on Bank of Japan expectations, NOT a carry-unwind panic.
